name: Phreesia
tagline: Patient intake, registration, insurance verification and payments for healthcare providers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Enterprise contracts, quoted per practice, not published.

verdictSummary: The visible part of Phreesia is a form wizard on a tablet, and yes, an agent can draft that before lunch. The part you cannot draft is everything behind the form: real-time eligibility and benefits checks against payer clearinghouses, card-present and card-on-file payments under PCI scope, bidirectional writeback into Epic, Cerner or athenahealth so the front desk never retypes anything, plus a BAA and the HIPAA posture that lets a compliance officer sign off. Those are contracts and certifications, not code. A personal replacement also makes no sense here: nobody intakes their own patients, this is bought by practices and health systems with audit requirements. Build the kiosk if you want to learn, but a clinic cannot run on it.
coreLoopDIY: A local tablet-friendly intake flow that collects demographics, consent signatures and insurance card photos, then prints or exports a PDF packet for manual entry.
requirements: A tablet or laptop at the front desk
A local machine to run it on, no cloud storage of health data
Somebody willing to retype everything into the actual EHR
A real BAA and HIPAA review if a single live patient ever touches it
whatYouLose: Real-time insurance eligibility and benefits verification through payer clearinghouses
Bidirectional EHR writeback, so your intake data stays trapped in a PDF
Integrated payments, copay collection, card on file and payment plans under PCI scope
HIPAA program, BAA, SOC 2, pen tests and the breach liability someone else is carrying
Appointment reminders, self-scheduling, waitlist and the whole pre-visit outreach layer
moatNotes: Eligibility checks mean payer connectivity, which means clearinghouse relationships. You cannot write your way into those.
whyPeopleStillPay: Practices do not buy Phreesia for the form UI, they buy it because the data lands in the EHR without the front desk touching a keyboard, because the copay gets collected before the visit, and because the insurance is verified before the patient sits down. Each of those is a revenue number, not a convenience. Add that a compliance officer needs a signed BAA and an audit trail, and the build-versus-buy conversation ends quickly. Even a small clinic is weighing a few hundred dollars a month against staff hours and denied claims.
notes: The questionnaire is a weekend; the plumbing is a procurement cycle. The moat is payer connectivity, EHR writeback and a signed BAA, none of which an agent can generate.
prompt:
Build a local, offline patient intake kiosk for a single small practice. This is a learning exercise and a paper-replacement tool, not a HIPAA-compliant system, and it must say so.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/intake.db
- pdf-lib for PDF generation
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost only, no auth provider, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics

Features in scope:
1. A JSON-defined form schema at ./forms/intake.json supporting field types: text, date, select, multiselect, yesno, signature, photo. Loading a different JSON file changes the whole questionnaire with no code edits.
2. A tablet-first, one-question-per-screen flow with large tap targets, a progress bar, and a back button. Works at 768px portrait.
3. Conditional logic: any field can declare `showIf: { field, equals }`.
4. Signature capture on a canvas, stored as a PNG blob in SQLite.
5. Insurance card capture via the device camera input, front and back, stored as blobs. No OCR, no parsing, no eligibility check: print a visible note that insurance must be verified manually.
6. On submit, generate a flat PDF packet of all answers plus signature and card images, and write a row to the `submissions` table.
7. A /staff page listing submissions with date, patient name, and buttons to download the PDF or delete the record. Protect it with a single passphrase from .env (STAFF_PASSPHRASE), checked server side.
8. A /kiosk route that auto-resets to a blank form 60 seconds after submit.

Explicitly out of scope, do not fake these:
- Any EHR, FHIR or HL7 integration
- Payer eligibility or benefits checks
- Card payments of any kind
- Patient accounts, logins or portals
- Any outbound network request whatsoever

Deliverables: the app, a .env.example with STAFF_PASSPHRASE, a README with setup steps, and a clear warning block in the README stating this stores health information unencrypted on a local disk and is not suitable for live patients without a security and compliance review.
